prompt: Nell left an ice cube on the warm porch step and went inside. When she came back, the ice cube had
options: frozen into a bigger block.
melted into a little puddle.
rolled off into the grass.

prompt: Finn pushed the swing much harder than before. The swing went
options: lower than it did before.
slower than it did before.
higher than it did before.

prompt: Cleo watered the dry plant every morning for a week. By the end of the week, the plant looked
options: green and strong.
dry and brown.
just the same as before.

prompt: The kitchen floor was wet in a ring around the sink. Most likely, someone had
options: tracked rain in through the door.
splashed water out of the sink.
spilled milk by the front door.

prompt: Juna's bike tire was flat this morning. The most likely reason is that the tire
options: had too much air pushed into it.
had been pumped up the night before.
had a small hole that let the air out.

prompt: All the lights in the house went dark at the same moment. This most likely happened because
options: the power to the whole house went out.
one old bulb in the hall burned out.
someone shut the door to the hall.

prompt: Bo dropped a glass onto the hard tile floor, and it broke into pieces. If the floor had been soft carpet instead, the glass most likely would have
options: broken into more pieces.
stayed in one piece.
made a much louder sound.

prompt: Iris ran the whole way to the bus stop and caught the bus just in time. If she had walked instead, she most likely would have
options: arrived before the bus came.
arrived just as the bus came.
arrived after the bus was gone.

prompt: Lars wants his ice pop to stay frozen until lunch. His best plan is to
options: keep it in the freezer until lunchtime.
hold it tightly in his warm hand.
set it on the sunny side of the table.

prompt: Suki's chalk drawings wash away every time it rains. If she wants her next drawing to last, she should draw it
options: with brighter colors of chalk.
under the roof where rain cannot reach.
early in the morning before school.

prompt: Petra hung her wet socks close to the fire and left her dry hat on the chair. After an hour by the fire, the socks were
options: colder and wetter.
just the same as before.
warm and dry.

prompt: The pond froze solid during a week of deep cold. When Wren stepped onto the ice with her sled, the ice
options: held her up without cracking.
broke and let her fall through.
melted under her warm boots.

prompt: Anya's sandwich was missing from the low table. Her dog stood nearby licking its lips, and her little brother was asleep upstairs the whole time. The sandwich was most likely eaten by
options: the brother asleep upstairs.
the dog beside the table.
a mouse from the cellar.

prompt: The plants on the left side of the garden grew tall, and the plants on the right side stayed short. The left side got sun all day, and both sides got the same water. The left plants most likely grew tall because of
options: the extra water on their side.
the softer soil on their side.
the extra sun on their side.

prompt: Colm's toy boat sank because he put it in the water before the glue had dried. If he had waited for the glue to dry first, the boat most likely would have
options: floated on top of the water.
sunk even faster than it did.
stuck to the bottom of the tub.

prompt: Yara studied the wrong page the night before the spelling test, so she missed most of the words. If she had studied the right page instead, she most likely would have
options: missed even more of the words.
spelled most of the words correctly.
run out of time on the test.

prompt: Rain fell hard all morning, and the dirt path turned to soft mud. When the wagon rolled onto the path, its wheels
options: rolled faster than before.
kicked up clouds of dust.
sank in and got stuck.

prompt: Jori left the freezer door open all night, and the freezer slowly warmed up inside. The ice in the trays turned to water, and by morning the water had
options: leaked out onto the kitchen floor.
frozen back into solid ice.
made the freezer colder than before.

prompt: Every night the raccoon tips over the trash can, and the loose lid falls off and the trash spills out. To stop the trash from spilling, the family should
options: paint the can a darker color.
strap the lid down tight.
fill the can right up to the top.

prompt: Nico's sandcastle falls down every afternoon when the waves reach it. Tomorrow he wants his castle to stand until night, so he should build it
options: closer to the water where the sand is wet.
taller and wider than the one today.
farther up the beach than the waves reach.

prompt: Wren set out three bowls of snow: one close to the fire, one by the open window, and one in the middle of the room. The fire was hot, and the air outside was freezing. An hour later, the only bowl that still held snow was the one
options: by the open window.
close to the fire.
in the middle of the room.

prompt: Before school, Tavi did three things: he fed the cat, he turned off every light, and he left the back door open a crack. All day an icy wind blew from the north. When Tavi came home, the kitchen felt
options: warmer than when he left.
colder than when he left.
exactly the same as when he left.

prompt: When Ruta got home, flour was spilled across the counter, small white paw prints led to the couch, and her cat lay asleep with white dust on its whiskers. Her dog had been out in the yard all day, and the window above the counter was shut tight. The flour was most likely spilled by
options: the dog that was out in the yard.
a gust of wind through the window.
the cat with dust on its whiskers.

prompt: The town's pond dropped a little lower every day for two weeks. It rained twice in that time, nobody took water from it, and the days were the hottest of the whole summer. The pond most likely dropped because the heat made the water
options: dry up into the air.
soak down into the mud.
run out through a crack.

prompt: On the way to the market, a bolt fell out of Essa's cart wheel, the wheel came off, and all her apples rolled into the ditch. That morning she had checked three of the four wheels but skipped the last one because she was late. If she had checked the last wheel too, her apples most likely would have
options: rolled into the ditch anyway.
reached the market safely in the cart.
been left at home that morning.

prompt: The school play needed music, lights, and costumes. Cass ran the music, Bea ran the lights, and the costumes were finished a month early. Halfway through the play, the stage went dark and the show had to stop. If Bea's job had gone right, the show most likely would have
options: stopped when the music failed.
stopped when a costume ripped.
gone on to the very end.

prompt: A heavy snow bent the power line, the bent line snapped, and the heater in the greenhouse shut off. The night that followed was bitterly cold. By morning, the flowers in the greenhouse had
options: frozen in the cold air.
wilted from too much heat.
grown taller in the dark.

prompt: Someone left the garden hose running, and the low corner of the yard slowly filled with water. The ants that lived in that corner marched out and moved into the dry doghouse. When the dog crawled into its house that night, it found
options: water pooling all over its bed.
ants crawling all over its bed.
its bed exactly as it always was.

prompt: The baker's cat chased a mouse across the counter and knocked the open salt shaker into the soup pot. The baker saw none of it and served the soup for lunch. The first person to taste the soup said it
options: needed a bit more salt.
was far too watery.
was far too salty.

prompt: Every winter, water gets into the crack in the front step, freezes at night, and pushes the crack wider. By spring the step is crumbling. To keep the step from crumbling next year, the best plan is to
options: fill the crack before winter comes.
pour warm water on the step each night.
sweep the snow off the step each morning.
